question: What are the key challenges, opportunities and directions of tool learning with foundation models, and how well can current models use tools?
hypothesis: Foundation models can use tools effectively with simple prompting, and training would help for hard tools.
contributions: A general tool learning framework (controller, tool set, environment, perceiver, human) and review of intent understanding, planning and training strategies
An experiment on 18 representative tools with text-davinci-003 and ChatGPT
Open-source BMTools repository integrating the tools
Discussion of safety, complex systems, tool creation, personalization, embodied learning, knowledge conflicts

method.summary: Survey with a small own experiment: 18 tools implemented in BMTools, each tested with text-davinci-003 and ChatGPT under no-tool, zero-shot (API docs) and few-shot (API docs plus usage examples) prompting. 12 tools use curated query sets judged on the API-call trace by humans; 6 use existing datasets with their own metrics.
method.task: tool use via prompting across 18 tools

datasets.name: MLQA (translator test)
datasets.preprocessing: English context, Arabian question, answer in English

datasets.name: ASDiv (calculator)
datasets.preprocessing: Text also names MathQA, but Table 1 lists only ASDiv

datasets.name: Database (curated)
datasets.size: 50 TPC-H queries, 2-6 tables, over 111.5 minutes to execute in total

other.size: not officially stated; authors speculate smaller than text-davinci-003

inference.prompting: Zero-shot: task description plus API information and basic guidelines. Few-shot: additionally concrete tool-use examples. ReAct-style Thought/Action/Observation format for most tools; one example in Appendix A per tool.

other.no_tool: run only where feasible; omitted for e.g. slides

metrics.name: accuracy
metrics.definition: ASDiv, RealTimeQA multiple choice, Stock, Database (ratio of queries with accurate results)

metrics.name: API-call trace correctness
metrics.definition: Curated sets: correct if humans judge all API calls accurate and the result reasonable. Slides: fraction of generated API calls executed without errors.

baselines: No Tool (model internal knowledge) where feasible
eval.protocol: Single run per cell (no seeds or variance reported); human judgement for curated sets with no rubric or rater count given; 4 people named for human evaluation in Contributions.

prompts.purpose: Weather API zero-shot vs few-shot illustration
prompts.text: Zero-shot Prompting: Here we provide a tool (API) "forecast_weather(city:str, N:int)", which could forecast the weather about a city on a specific date (after N days from today). The returned information covers "temperature", "wind", and "precipitation". Please write codes using this tool to answer the following question: "What's the average temperature in Beijing next week?"

You are a helpful assistant to make multiple choices. You have access to several APIs: (1) Search(query:str)... (2) LoadPage(idx:int)... Generate ONLY one piece of thought and one piece of action/answer each time, do not give more! Keep your response succinct and no more than one line.

evidence.quote: The results of text-davinci-003 are shown on white background, while the results of ChatGPT are shown in cyan background.

results.claim: The authors evaluate 18 tools with two models under no-tool, zero-shot and few-shot prompting.
results.setup: text-davinci-003 and ChatGPT (Mar 23, 2023 version), prompting only; Table 1
results.quote: We select 18 representative tools for evaluation and place the main results in this section.

results.claim: Zero-shot tool use can score below no tool where the model can use internal knowledge; few-shot tool use is claimed to always beat no tool.
results.setup: text-davinci-003 and ChatGPT (Mar 23, 2023 version), prompting only
results.note: Table 1 contradicts 'consistently' for ChatGPT on Wikipedia/HotpotQA: no tool 34.5, few-shot 19.0.
results.quote: utilizing tools with zero-shot prompting could sometimes lead to worse performance, which implies that sub-optimal utilization of tools may negatively impact performance. Nevertheless, incorporating tools with few-shot prompting still consistently yields superior performance than not incorporating tools.

results.claim: ChatGPT Calculator/ASDiv accuracy: no tool 91.7, zero-shot 74.1, few-shot 92.5.
results.setup: text-davinci-003 and ChatGPT (Mar 23, 2023 version), prompting only; ASDiv, 266 test items; ChatGPT row
results.note: Text extraction interleaves the two model rows; row assignment taken from the row ordering (text-davinci-003 first, ChatGPT second) as the caption states.
results.table: Table 1, row Calculator (ASDiv), ChatGPT zero-shot (74.1) vs no tool (91.7), few-shot 92.5

results.claim: ChatGPT Wikipedia/HotpotQA: no tool 34.5, zero-shot 8.5, few-shot 19.0 (tool use hurts).
results.setup: text-davinci-003 and ChatGPT (Mar 23, 2023 version), prompting only; HotpotQA open-domain, 200 sampled; ChatGPT row
results.table: Table 1, row Wikipedia (HotpotQA), ChatGPT few-shot column (19.0); no tool 34.5; zero-shot 8.5

results.claim: ChatGPT Search Engine/RealTimeQA: no tool 50.0, zero-shot 43.3, few-shot 63.3.
results.setup: text-davinci-003 and ChatGPT (Mar 23, 2023 version), prompting only; RealTimeQA 20230217 multiple choice, 30 items
results.table: Table 1, row Search Engine (RealTimeQA), ChatGPT few-shot column (63.3); no tool 50.0; zero-shot 43.3

results.claim: Tools whose parameter is executable code (KGs SPARQL) stay hard; KGs few-shot 46.9 (davinci) and 14.1 (ChatGPT).
results.setup: text-davinci-003 and ChatGPT (Mar 23, 2023 version), prompting only; KGs, 64 curated questions, 7 APIs
results.quote: tools requiring the generation of executable code as the parameter to the API, such as the search_by_query API in the KGs tool (see Appendix A.9 for more details), are found to be significantly more arduous.
results.table: Table 1, row KGs (Curated), ChatGPT few-shot column (14.1); text-davinci-003 few-shot 46.9

results.claim: Map, Weather, Slides, Tables, Cooking Assistant and AI Painting reach satisfying completion rates few-shot (e.g. Weather 99.0 for both models).
results.setup: text-davinci-003 and ChatGPT (Mar 23, 2023 version), prompting only; Weather, 100 curated queries, few-shot
results.quote: certain tools such as Map, Weather, Slides, Tables, Cooking Assistant, and AI Painting exhibit a satisfying completion rate.
results.table: Table 1, row Weather (Curated), few-shot columns (99.0 both models)

results.claim: Several tools remain far from satisfactory with few-shot prompting: KGs, Wikipedia, online shopping, 3D model construction.
results.setup: text-davinci-003 and ChatGPT (Mar 23, 2023 version), prompting only
results.quote: However, for several tools such as KGs, Wikipedia, online shopping, and 3D model construction, the model performance is still far from satisfactory even with few-shot prompting.

results.claim: ChatGPT does not beat text-davinci-003 despite RLHF; authors attribute it to alignment tax and a possibly smaller model (speculation, untested).
results.setup: text-davinci-003 and ChatGPT (Mar 23, 2023 version), prompting only
results.quote: although ChatGPT has been fine-tuned with RLHF, it does not yield better results than text-davinci-003.

results.claim: Scores across tools are not comparable because setups differ.
results.quote: it is important to acknowledge that the evaluation setups of these tools are inherently different, making direct comparison difficult.

results.claim: Curated test sets are scored on the API-call trace judged by humans, not on a final-answer metric.
results.setup: 12 tools with curated queries (seeded by hand, expanded by ChatGPT in-context, hand-filtered)
results.quote: for these manually curated test sets, we employ the trace of API calls as the metric for evaluating the models' performance. Specifically, if humans judge that all the API calls are accurate for the given task, and they yield a reasonable result, the task is deemed to be correctly completed.

results.claim: Environment feedback splits into result feedback (task success) and intermediate feedback (state change per action).
results.quote: result feedback, which is ultimate feedback returned from the environment

results.claim: Tool-use performance is proposed as a next-generation gauge of machine intelligence; no benchmark given.
results.quote: We contend that the tool learning performance can serve as a next-generation gauge for measuring machine intelligence

results.claim: In a hand-run case, ChatGPT corrected its own answer (13 to 14 Champions League titles) when given Wikipedia output, and flagged a Wikipedia/Bing conflict.
results.quote: We find that ChatGPT is able to correct its own belief given retrieved information and discern the knowledge conflicts from different sources.

limits: Test sets are small (3D n=10, AI Painting n=25, RealTimeQA n=30, Cooking n=50, Database n=50) with no variance, seeds or repeated runs.
Curated-set scoring relies on unspecified human judgement of 'accurate' API calls; no rubric, rater count or agreement.
Curated queries were expanded with ChatGPT, which is also a model under test; circularity not discussed.
Authors concede metrics differ per tool so cross-tool comparison is difficult (p.25).
Text and Table 1 disagree: Calculator text names ASDiv and MathQA but the table has only ASDiv; Stock text says 1200 question-answer pairs, table test size 122.
Table 1 text extraction interleaves the two model rows; ChatGPT-versus-davinci assignment rests on row order and the caption.
Models are text-davinci-003 and ChatGPT (Mar 23, 2023); predates native function calling. Reasons offered for ChatGPT trailing davinci (alignment tax, size) are untested.

Appendix case studies show one trace per tool, apparently successes; some traces contain unremarked errors (online shopping clicks the demo item ID; search trace calls undocumented search_top3 and load_page_index).
practices: Unify tool interfaces (semantic, GUI or programming interface) to enable generalization (Sec 3.3.3).
Add a tool-selection retrieval stage when the tool set exceeds the context (Sec 3.2.1).
Use few-shot usage examples rather than API descriptions alone for tool understanding (Sec 4.2).
Evaluate trained tool-use on feedback at result and intermediate level (Sec 3.3.2).

terms.definition: Combining the strengths of specialized tools and foundation models for greater accuracy, efficiency and autonomy in problem-solving.
Generating a static multi-step plan for tool use without interacting with the environment.
Generating plans incrementally by iteratively interacting with the environment and using feedback.
Ultimate feedback from the environment indicating whether the actions completed the task.
The state change of the environment triggered by an action.
